Requirement Description: The sim shall let the user select the parent body model from an enumerated list.
Acceptance Criteria: Each enum value loads and propagates without error.

Requirement Description: The sim shall model the parent body as a sphere of uniform density.
Acceptance Criteria: Accel matches mu/r^2 to 1e-12 relative.
Comments: mu = G x mass of the parent. mu/r^2 is textbook gravity at distance r from the centre. 1e-12 relative means the two numbers agree to about 12 digits.

Requirement Description: The sim shall model Earth as the WGS84 ellipsoid with zonal gravity to J4, rotation, exponential atmosphere and dipole magnetic field.
Acceptance Criteria: SSO RAAN drift 0.9856 deg/day ±0.5%; g at equator 9.780 m/s^2 ±0.001.
Comments: WGS84 is the standard Earth shape used by GPS. J2 to J4 are correction terms for Earth's equatorial bulge and north-south lopsidedness. SSO RAAN drift: a sun-synchronous orbit's plane must rotate 0.9856 deg/day to keep pace with the Sun, which is a good check that the J2 term is right.

Input/Output: .obj file, length unit (m or km), density (kg/m^3)
Requirement Description: The sim shall model the parent body as a closed triangular mesh of uniform density using polyhedron gravity.
Acceptance Criteria: Sphere mesh matches point mass within mesh volume error; div(g) = 0 outside the body.
Comments: Polyhedron gravity computes exact gravity of a mesh-shaped body, valid right down to the surface. div(g) = 0 outside is a physics law any correct gravity field must obey, so it is a built-in self-check.

Requirement Description: The sim shall reject meshes that are not closed or manifold, with an error naming the defect.
Acceptance Criteria: Open-mesh test case raises an error naming the open edges.
Comments: Closed: no holes. Manifold: every edge is shared by exactly 2 triangles. Gravity and volume are wrong for meshes that break either rule.

Input/Output: spin period (s), pole RA and Dec (deg), prime meridian angle at epoch (deg)
Requirement Description: The sim shall model the parent as rotating uniformly about a user-set pole at a user-set rate. Fixed by constants for earth_default.
Acceptance Criteria: A body-fixed point returns to its start inertial position after one period within 1e-9 relative.
Comments: Pole RA/Dec: direction of the spin axis, given like a star's sky coordinates. Prime meridian angle: how far the body has rotated at the start time, i.e. where its "longitude zero" points.

Requirement Description: The sim shall render the parent shape to scale in the inertial frame, rotating at its spin rate.
Acceptance Criteria: Rendered extents match shape model within 1%; orientation after one period matches start.
Comments: Inertial frame: a non-rotating reference frame fixed relative to the stars.

Requirement Description: The sim shall model each satellite as a point mass. Satellites share one mass and shape by default, with per-satellite overrides allowed by SIM_027, SIM_028 and SIM_039.
Acceptance Criteria: Mass <= 0 or > 10000 kg is rejected with an error.

Requirement Description: The sim shall convert the .stp file to a decimated mesh for display only, with no effect on the physics.
Acceptance Criteria: Trajectory with and without .stp is identical.
Comments: Decimated mesh: the CAD model simplified to far fewer triangles so it renders fast.

Requirement Description: The sim shall show the decimated satellite model orbiting the parent when a .stp is provided.
Acceptance Criteria: Model is displayed at the propagated position at every frame.

Requirement Description: The sim shall show each satellite as a small sphere orbiting the parent when no .stp is provided.
Acceptance Criteria: Sphere is displayed at the propagated position at every frame.

Requirement Description: The sim shall propagate N satellites in one run.
Acceptance Criteria: N = 1 to 100 runs without error; N < 1 or > 100 raises an error.
Comments: Propagate: compute the satellite's position and velocity forward in time.

Requirement Description: The sim shall name each satellite individually, or auto-name them as prefix-01, prefix-02, and so on.
Acceptance Criteria: Duplicate names raise an error.

Requirement Description: The sim shall accept the start epoch as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit time scale.
Acceptance Criteria: Same instant in each scale converts to identical internal time within 1 us.
Comments: Epoch: a specific instant in time. UTC is civil time with leap seconds. TAI, TT, TDB and GPS are atomic or astronomical time scales that differ from UTC by tens of seconds, so the scale must be stated.

Input/Output: seconds or ISO 8601 duration; or end epoch per SIM_014
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept the run length as a duration or an end epoch, not both.
Acceptance Criteria: Supplying both raises an error.
Comments: ISO 8601 duration example: P1DT6H means 1 day 6 hours.

Requirement Description: The sim shall propagate with a fixed-step RK4 integrator using a user-set step size.
Acceptance Criteria: Fixed-step run uses exactly the given step.
Comments: RK4 (Runge-Kutta 4th order): the standard simple method for stepping equations of motion forward in time.

Requirement Description: The sim shall offer an adaptive-step integrator controlled by user-set rtol and atol.
Acceptance Criteria: 1-day LEO run at rtol 1e-10 matches rtol 1e-12 run within 1 m.
Comments: DOP853: a high-accuracy integrator that picks its own step size. rtol/atol: allowed error per step, relative (fraction of the value) and absolute (in metres or m/s).

Requirement Description: The sim shall output states at a user-set interval independent of the integration step.
Acceptance Criteria: Output timestamps spaced exactly as set.
Comments: State: a satellite's position and velocity at one instant.

Input/Output: osculating Keplerian elements: a (m), e, i, RAAN, argument of periapsis, true anomaly (deg)
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept a satellite's initial orbit as osculating Keplerian elements in the parent's inertial frame at start_epoch.
Acceptance Criteria: Elements to state vector to elements round trip within 1e-9 relative.
Comments: The 6 numbers describing an orbit. a: size. e: how stretched (0 = circle). i: tilt from the equator. RAAN: where the orbit crosses the equator going north. Argument of periapsis: where the lowest point is. True anomaly: where the satellite is on the orbit. Osculating: the exact instantaneous values, not averaged ones like in a TLE.

Input/Output: state vector: x, y, z (m), vx, vy, vz (m/s)
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept a satellite's initial state as an inertial position and velocity vector at start_epoch.
Acceptance Criteria: Equivalent Keplerian and Cartesian inputs give identical trajectories.
Comments: Needed because Keplerian elements break down for circular or equatorial orbits, where some angles become undefined.

Input/Output: list of N initial states per SIM_019 or SIM_020
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept a separate initial orbit for each satellite.
Acceptance Criteria: List length not equal to N raises an error.

Input/Output: Walker pattern i:T/P/F; a (m), reference RAAN and true anomaly (deg)
Requirement Description: The sim shall generate initial orbits for N = T satellites from a Walker delta pattern.
Acceptance Criteria: Generated RAANs spaced 360/P deg and phasing matches F to 1e-9 deg.
Comments: Walker pattern: standard constellation layout. i = inclination, T = total satellites, P = number of orbital planes, F = phasing offset between neighbouring planes. Example: 53:24/3/1.

Input/Output: base orbit; offsets in RAAN, true anomaly (deg) or along-track distance (m)
Requirement Description: The sim shall generate initial orbits for a train of satellites from one base orbit and a fixed offset.
Acceptance Criteria: Satellite k has offset k times the input offset.
Comments: Train: satellites following each other in the same orbit, evenly spaced. Along-track: direction of travel.

Requirement Description: The sim shall find the lowest circular orbit radius, at a user-set inclination, for which the satellite neither impacts the surface nor exceeds R_max over the run duration.
Acceptance Criteria: Returned orbit survives the full run; an orbit 1% lower impacts or escapes.
Comments: Around irregular bodies, low orbits get pushed around by the lumpy gravity and can crash or fly off. R_max is the distance beyond which the satellite counts as escaped.

Requirement Description: The sim shall compute satellite acceleration from the gravity of the selected parent model.
Acceptance Criteria: Circular orbit around sphere_uniform keeps constant radius within 1e-6 relative over 10 orbits.
Comments: Force model: the list of forces acting on the satellite.

Input/Output: drag, SRP, Sun/Moon third body on/off
Requirement Description: The sim shall let the user enable drag, solar radiation pressure and third-body gravity individually.
Acceptance Criteria: Each force changes the trajectory only when enabled.
Comments: Drag: air resistance from the thin upper atmosphere. SRP (solar radiation pressure): tiny push from sunlight. Third body: gravity of the Sun and Moon.

Input/Output: Cd, area (m^2), default or per satellite
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept drag parameters per satellite so differential drag can be modelled.
Acceptance Criteria: Equal values give zero differential drag; unequal values give growing along-track separation.
Comments: Cd: drag coefficient, about 2.2 for satellites. Differential drag: two satellites feeling different drag, so they slowly drift apart. Also usable on purpose to steer formations without fuel.

Input/Output: Cr, area (m^2), default or per satellite
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept SRP parameters per satellite so differential SRP can be modelled.
Acceptance Criteria: Equal values give zero differential SRP acceleration.
Comments: Cr: reflectivity coefficient, 1 = absorbs all light, 2 = mirror.

Requirement Description: The sim shall treat satellites as independent, with no mutual gravity or interaction, unless SIM_030 is enabled.
Acceptance Criteria: Each satellite's trajectory is identical whether run alone or with the others.

Requirement Description: The sim shall optionally include gravity between satellites.
Acceptance Criteria: Two satellites at rest 10 m apart accelerate per G*m/r^2 within 1e-9 relative.
Comments: Usually negligible: two 100 kg satellites 10 m apart pull each other at about 7e-11 m/s^2. Matters only for very close, long-duration formations.

Requirement Description: The sim shall let the user designate one satellite as chief and define the others (deputies) relative to it.
Acceptance Criteria: Unknown chief name raises an error.
Comments: Chief: the reference satellite. Deputies: the others in the formation, described by where they are relative to the chief.

Input/Output: deputy position (m) and velocity (m/s) in chief LVLH (radial, along-track, cross-track)
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept each deputy's initial state relative to the chief in the chief's LVLH frame.
Acceptance Criteria: LVLH to inertial to LVLH round trip within 1 mm and 1 um/s.
Comments: LVLH (local vertical, local horizontal): a frame that rides with the chief. Radial = straight up away from the parent, along-track = direction of travel, cross-track = sideways out of the orbit plane.

Input/Output: relative orbital elements: da, dlambda, dex, dey, dix, diy
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept each deputy's initial state as quasi-nonsingular relative orbital elements.
Acceptance Criteria: ROE to inertial to ROE round trip within 1e-9 relative.
Comments: ROE: the difference between the deputy's and chief's orbits, in 6 numbers. Easier to design formations with because each number maps to a visible feature: da = drift, dlambda = along-track offset, de = in-plane ellipse, di = cross-track motion. Quasi-nonsingular: still works for circular orbits.

Requirement Description: The sim shall adjust deputy initial velocity to remove along-track drift relative to the chief under two-body gravity.
Acceptance Criteria: Along-track drift under 1 mm per orbit in a two-body run.
Comments: If a deputy's orbit is even slightly larger or smaller than the chief's, it has a different period and drifts away every orbit. This sets the deputy's velocity so both periods match. Two-body: gravity of a perfect sphere only.

Requirement Description: The sim shall adjust deputy initial conditions to remove secular J2 drift relative to the chief.
Acceptance Criteria: Along-track drift under 1 m per day with earth_default gravity.
Comments: Secular: steadily growing, as opposed to oscillating. Earth's bulge (J2) rotates orbits at slightly different rates if they differ in size, shape or tilt. This picks deputy orbits whose J2 rates match the chief's, so the formation holds.

Requirement Description: The sim shall propagate every satellite with the full force model and derive relative motion from the difference, not from linearised equations.
Acceptance Criteria: For a 100 m formation in two-body gravity, matches HCW solution within 2 mm after one orbit.
Comments: HCW (Hill-Clohessy-Wiltshire): simplified textbook equations for relative motion, accurate only for close formations in circular orbits. Used here only as a check, not to run the sim.

Requirement Description: The sim shall propagate all satellites on a common time grid so relative position error stays below 1 cm over one day.
Acceptance Criteria: Two identical satellites with zero separation stay within 1e-6 m over one day.
Comments: Satellites are ~7000 km from Earth's centre but may be only metres apart. If each gets its own step sizes, small numerical errors don't cancel and show up as fake relative motion.

Input/Output: per satellite: epoch, delta-v vector (m/s), frame (LVLH or inertial)
Requirement Description: The sim shall apply user-scheduled impulsive maneuvers to any satellite.
Acceptance Criteria: Velocity changes by the commanded delta-v at the commanded epoch within 1e-9 m/s.
Comments: Delta-v: change in velocity from a thruster burn. Impulsive: treated as instant, a good approximation for short burns.

Input/Output: thrust (N), Isp (s), start epoch, duration (s), direction
Requirement Description: The sim shall model finite-duration burns with propellant mass depletion.
Acceptance Criteria: Achieved delta-v matches the rocket equation within 0.1%.
Comments: Isp (specific impulse): fuel efficiency of the thruster; higher means less propellant per delta-v. Rocket equation: the standard formula linking delta-v, Isp and propellant mass.

Input/Output: control box per deputy (m in R, T, N); controller on/off
Requirement Description: The sim shall hold each deputy inside a user-set box around its target LVLH position using closed-loop impulsive control.
Acceptance Criteria: Deputy stays inside the box for the full run; every burn logged.
Comments: Station keeping: small periodic burns to stay at a target position. R, T, N = radial, along-track, cross-track. Closed-loop: the controller watches the position and fires only when the deputy drifts toward the box edge.

Requirement Description: When a satellite reaches the parent surface, the sim shall stop propagating that satellite, continue the others, and report impact epoch and location.
Acceptance Criteria: Trajectory aimed at the surface stops with impact epoch within 1 s; other satellites unaffected.
Comments: Body-fixed: coordinates that rotate with the parent, like latitude and longitude on Earth.

Requirement Description: The sim shall flag every epoch where two satellites come closer than a user-set distance.
Acceptance Criteria: Test case with a known crossing is flagged within one output step.

Requirement Description: The sim shall flag every epoch where a deputy enters a keep-out sphere around the chief.
Acceptance Criteria: Test case with a known entry is flagged within one output step.
Comments: Keep-out sphere: a safety zone around the chief that deputies must never enter.

Requirement Description: The sim shall report the drift of the conserved energy (Jacobi constant for rotating parents) over the run.
Acceptance Criteria: Gravity-only 1-day run drifts less than 1e-8 relative.
Comments: With gravity only, orbital energy should stay exactly constant. Any drift is numerical error, so it's the best overall health check. Jacobi constant: the equivalent conserved quantity when the parent body is rotating.

Input/Output: plan.csv: sat_name, epoch (ISO 8601 UTC), t (s), x, y, z (m), vx, vy, vz (m/s) inertial, parent rotation angle (deg)
Requirement Description: The sim shall write every satellite's state and the parent orientation at every output step to plan.csv.
Acceptance Criteria: Every satellite has one row per output step; reloading reproduces states within 1 mm.
Comments: Parent rotation angle: how far the parent has spun, so the visualization can show the surface turning under the orbit.

Input/Output: body-fixed x, y, z (m); lat, lon (deg), alt (m)
Requirement Description: The sim shall add body-fixed and geodetic position columns to plan.csv.
Acceptance Criteria: Geodetic columns match WGS84 conversion within 1 mm for earth_default.
Comments: Geodetic: latitude, longitude and altitude measured on the WGS84 ellipsoid, same as GPS coordinates.

Input/Output: plan.csv columns per deputy: LVLH position (m), velocity (m/s), ROE
Requirement Description: The sim shall output each deputy's relative state in the chief LVLH frame and as ROE at every output step.
Acceptance Criteria: LVLH output matches difference of inertial states rotated to LVLH within 1 mm.
Comments: See SIM_032 for LVLH and SIM_033 for ROE.

Requirement Description: The sim shall output the range and line of sight between each satellite pair at every output step.
Acceptance Criteria: Range matches distance computed from plan.csv positions within 1 mm.
Comments: Line of sight: true if the parent body isn't blocking the straight line between two satellites. Matters for inter-satellite links.

Requirement Description: The sim shall report the minimum radial/cross-track separation per deputy per orbit.
Acceptance Criteria: Matches separation computed from LVLH output within 1 mm.
Comments: Passive safety: if thrusters fail, along-track position drifts unpredictably but radial (R) and cross-track (N) separation stay structured. Keeping R-N separation above zero means satellites can't collide even with no control.

Input/Output: delta-v (m/s) and propellant used (kg) per satellite
Requirement Description: The sim shall report cumulative delta-v and propellant use per satellite.
Acceptance Criteria: Sum of logged burns equals reported total.
Comments: Delta-v budget: total velocity change spent, which sets how much propellant the mission needs.

Requirement Description: The sim shall animate plan.csv over time, showing all satellites and the rotating parent together.
Acceptance Criteria: Displayed epoch matches the CSV rows being shown.

Requirement Description: The sim shall show each satellite with its own colour and name label.
Acceptance Criteria: All N satellites are visible and distinguishable at every frame.

Requirement Description: The sim shall offer a chief-centred LVLH view showing deputy relative trajectories.
Acceptance Criteria: Plotted deputy positions match LVLH output at every frame.
Comments: View from the chief's point of view. Deputies trace loops and ellipses around it instead of whole orbits.

Requirement Description: The sim shall let the user change playback speed, pause and scrub the animation.
Acceptance Criteria: Playback at each speed advances epoch at the selected rate within 1%.

Requirement Description: The sim shall read all inputs from one config file and record the config and sim version in every output.
Acceptance Criteria: Rerunning a saved config reproduces plan.csv exactly.

Requirement Description: The sim shall complete a 1-day LEO run of 1 satellite (sphere_uniform, RK4, 10 s step) in under 10 s on a standard laptop.
Acceptance Criteria: Measured run time under 10 s.

Requirement Description: The sim shall complete a 1-day LEO run of 100 satellites (sphere_uniform, RK4, 10 s step) in under 5 min on a standard laptop.
Acceptance Criteria: Measured run time under 5 min.

Input/Output: heliocentric Keplerian elements of the parent at epoch (Sun-centred, ecliptic J2000); or SPICE SPK file + body ID
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept the parent body's orbit around the Sun when parent_shape is sphere_uniform or custom.
Acceptance Criteria: For a known asteroid (e.g. Bennu), Sun direction from the parent matches JPL Horizons within 1e-5 rad over 30 days.
Comments: Needed so the sim knows where the Sun is, for SRP, Sun gravity and eclipses. SPICE is NASA's standard toolkit for planet and spacecraft positions; an SPK file is its position data file. JPL Horizons is NASA's online ephemeris service, used here as truth.

Requirement Description: The sim shall compute Sun and Moon positions relative to Earth from the JPL DE440 ephemeris for earth_default.
Acceptance Criteria: Sun and Moon positions match JPL Horizons within 1 km.
Comments: Ephemeris: a table of where solar-system bodies are over time. DE440 is JPL's current standard. de440s is the smaller version covering 1849 to 2150.

Input/Output: leap-second file (NAIF naif0012.tls or IERS Bulletin C)
Requirement Description: The sim shall read leap seconds from a versioned data file that can be updated without changing code.
Acceptance Criteria: UTC to TAI offset is 37 s for 2026 epochs; replacing the file changes the offset accordingly.
Comments: Leap seconds are occasionally added to UTC. A wrong or outdated table shifts every UTC epoch by 1 s, which is about 7.5 km of orbit position in LEO.

Input/Output: F10.7 and Ap: fixed user values, or CelesTrak space weather file
Requirement Description: The sim shall accept solar flux and geomagnetic indices for atmospheric density when an atmosphere model other than exponential is used.
Acceptance Criteria: Fixed values reproduce reference density within 1%; file input uses the value for each epoch.
Comments: F10.7: solar radio flux, a proxy for how much the Sun heats the upper atmosphere. Ap: geomagnetic activity index. Both swing drag by a factor of 10 over the solar cycle.

Requirement Description: The sim shall record the name, version and checksum of every data file used in each run's output.
Acceptance Criteria: Output lists every data file loaded; changing a file changes the recorded checksum.
Comments: Makes runs reproducible: you can tell later exactly which ephemeris and leap-second files produced a result.

Requirement Description: The sim shall compute a shadow factor from 0 (full shadow) to 1 (full sun) and scale SRP by it.
Acceptance Criteria: For a circular equatorial orbit, eclipse entry and exit match the analytic solution within 1 s.
Comments: Cylindrical: Earth's shadow as a simple tube, on or off. Conical: models the real cone-shaped shadow, including penumbra (partial shadow) for a few seconds at entry and exit.

Input/Output: shadow factor column in plan.csv; eclipse entry and exit epochs and durations
Requirement Description: The sim shall output the shadow factor at every output step and a list of eclipse events per satellite.
Acceptance Criteria: Event times match the shadow factor crossing 0.5 within one output step.
Comments: Also directly useful for power budget analysis: time in eclipse sets battery depth of discharge.

Requirement Description: The sim shall compute shadowing by a custom parent from its mesh shape, or from an equal-volume sphere if the user selects sphere.
Acceptance Criteria: Mesh shadowing of a sphere mesh matches sphere shadowing within 1 s per eclipse.
Comments: Irregular asteroids cast irregular shadows. Mesh shadowing traces a ray from satellite to Sun and checks whether it hits the mesh.

Input/Output: GCRF for earth_default; ICRF axes centred on parent centre of mass otherwise
Requirement Description: The sim shall define the inertial frame as ICRF-aligned axes centred on the parent's centre of mass.
Acceptance Criteria: Frame name and centre recorded in every output file.
Comments: ICRF: the international standard non-rotating frame, fixed relative to distant quasars. GCRF is the same axes centred on Earth. Same idea as J2000, but more precisely defined.

Input/Output: earth_default: IAU 2006/2000A precession-nutation + Earth rotation angle; polar motion optional
Requirement Description: The sim shall convert between inertial and Earth-fixed coordinates using the IAU 2006/2000A model.
Acceptance Criteria: Earth-fixed positions match ERFA or Astropy within 1 m at the surface.
Comments: Earth's spin axis wobbles slowly. Precession alone moves it about 0.36 deg between 2000 and 2026, which shifts ground tracks by tens of km if ignored. ERFA is the open-source standard library implementing these models.

Input/Output: custom and sphere_uniform: pole and rotation per SIM_006, defined in ICRF
Requirement Description: The sim shall define the parent body-fixed frame from the pole and rotation in SIM_006, with the pole given in ICRF.
Acceptance Criteria: Body-fixed to inertial to body-fixed round trip within 1e-9 relative.

Input/Output: CSV header naming frame and units per column
Requirement Description: The sim shall state the frame and unit of every output column in the file header.
Acceptance Criteria: Every numeric column has a frame (where applicable) and unit label.
Comments: Prevents the most common analysis bug: mixing inertial and body-fixed coordinates.

Input/Output: Python 3.11+; NumPy, SciPy, spiceypy, ERFA; open-source dependencies only
Requirement Description: The sim shall be written in Python 3.11 or later using only open-source libraries.
Acceptance Criteria: Clean install from the dependency list runs all tests.
Comments: spiceypy: Python wrapper for NASA SPICE.

Requirement Description: The sim shall run on Linux, macOS and Windows.
Acceptance Criteria: Test suite passes on all three.

Requirement Description: The sim shall run from the command line given a config file per SIM_055.
Acceptance Criteria: A run with a valid config completes and writes all outputs with no other input.

Requirement Description: The sim shall be importable as a Python library so runs can be scripted and batched.
Acceptance Criteria: Same config through CLI and API gives identical plan.csv.
Comments: Useful for parameter sweeps, e.g. 100 runs at different altitudes.

Requirement Description: The sim shall provide a 3D viewer that runs in a standard web browser with no installation.
Acceptance Criteria: Viewer opens plan.csv from any SIM_055 run in Chrome, Firefox and Safari.
Comments: Implements the visualization rows (SIM_007, SIM_010, SIM_011, SIM_051 to SIM_054). three.js is the standard library for 3D in the browser.

Input/Output: static plots (PNG): altitude vs time, ground track, LVLH relative motion, eclipse timeline
Requirement Description: The sim shall generate static summary plots for each run.
Acceptance Criteria: One plot file per type is created for every run that has the relevant data.
Comments: Quick look without opening the 3D viewer. Ground track: the path of the satellite's point directly below it on the surface.
